q: run a focused campaign funnel drill for the top 10 campaigns (LPV → sessions → add_to_carts → orders → contribution_margin / ROAS) to confirm per-campaign conversion rates and isolate whether audience, creative or landing UX is driving low efficiency.
answer:
Short answer: Two Meta campaigns — TH-383-SUSPENDER-29SEP and TH-383-SUSPENDER-26SEP-ADV+ — look like the main sources of low-intent traffic (many LPVs/sessions but few orders and very low ROAS); among the top‑10 spenders only [Google Build] PMax - Seasonal New shows a clearly positive net ROAS (1.2x) and the largest contribution margin.

Key evidence (Campaigns = top 10 by ad spend, 1–13 Oct)
- TH-383-SUSPENDER-29SEP — Ad spend ₹49,163 · LPVs 3,356 · Sessions 4,192 · Add-to-carts 200 · Orders 20 · Contribution margin ₹21,739 · Net ROAS 0.4 → Many landing views/sessions but poor conversion and ROAS (low-intent/low-efficiency).
- TH-383-SUSPENDER-26SEP-ADV+ — Ad spend ₹55,793 · LPVs 2,546 · Sessions 2,400 · Add-to-carts 189 · Orders 22 · Contribution margin ₹22,116 · Net ROAS 0.4 → same pattern as above.
- [Google Build] PMax - Seasonal New — Ad spend ₹50,646 · Sessions 3,325 · Add-to-carts 704 · Orders 65 · Contribution margin ₹62,747 · Net ROAS 1.2 → high add-to-cart funnel and the only top‑10 campaign with ROAS >1.
- Others (Brand Search, Wingbird, PawTech, Scratchlounge) show moderate sessions and add‑to‑carts but net ROAS <1 (contribution margins positive but not enough vs spend). Several campaigns (notably Google demand gen) have no LPV rows here — No data available for LPV (platform mismatch).

What this says about your hypotheses
- Broader / lower‑intent audiences: supported for the two TH-383 campaigns (high LPVs/sessions but low orders and ROAS — classic low‑intent signal).
- Creative / landing mismatch or UX friction: plausible for the same two campaigns (high LPVs but low add-to-cart → landing or creative relevance issue). The data does not yet single out creative vs landing; we have evidence pointing to an LPV → sessions → add-to-cart drop.
- Higher volume UX friction under load: not supported by these numbers alone — sessions are higher, but conversion drops are concentrated in specific campaigns rather than site-wide.

Period: 2026-10-01..2026-10-13 · Currency: INR · Data as of 2026-10-14

Next: Want me to drill those two low-intent campaigns by creative and landing page (LPV → add_to_cart → orders) so we can tell whether the problem is the creative targeting or the landing UX?
